primitives.name: Interaction Information
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model **Interaction information (Algorithm 1):** τ_ij = I(F_i; F_j; Y) = I(F_i; F_j | Y) - I(F_i; F_j) = H(F_i,F_j) + H(F_j,Y) + H(F_i,Y) - H(F_i) - H(F_j) - H(Y) - H(F_i,F_j,Y).
primitives.latex: \tau_{ij} = I(F_i; F_j; Y) = I(F_i; F_j | Y) - I(F_i; F_j) = H(F_i,F_j) + H(F_j,Y) + H(F_i,Y) - H(F_i) - H(F_j) - H(Y) - H(F_i,F_j,Y)
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'τ_ij': 'dimensionless synergy measure between features F_i and F_j given target Y', 'I(·; ·; ·)': 'mutual information among three variables', 'H(·)': 'entropy of a variable or joint distribution'}
primitives.assumptions: Features are discrete or discretizable, mutual information estimable via nearest neighbor methods, target variable known.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When entropy estimates become unreliable due to small sample size or high cardinality.

layer2.mapping: τ_ij induces a symmetric similarity matrix over feature pairs, enabling graph-based feature selection and kernel construction for downstream models.
layer2.telemetry: Cross-validated performance gain from selected feature pairs

primitives.name: IIFE Feature Engineering
primitives.verbatim_quote: **IIFE (Algorithm 3):** (1) compute II for all pairs (O(|F|2); prefilter to F̃ = top-50 by RF impurity importance if |F| too large); (2) loop: take K highest-τ pairs, apply all bivariate functions B, evaluate each candidate
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'K': 'integer number of top τ pairs considered per iteration', 'B': 'set of bivariate transformation functions', 'U': 'set of univariate transformation functions', 'F̃': 'prefiltered subset of features based on RF importance'}
primitives.assumptions: Feature transformations are computationally tractable, model performance measurable via cross-validation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When computational budget exceeds O(|F|²) or when feature interactions are too sparse to detect reliably.

layer2.mapping: IIFE constructs a derived kernel from τ_ij values, enabling non-linear feature combinations without exhaustive search.
layer2.telemetry: Number of generated features and their downstream model accuracy

primitives.name: Patience Stopping Criterion
primitives.verbatim_quote: Stop: patience P — stop if mean of recent P/2 CV scores ≤ mean of previous P/2 (Algorithm 2).

primitives.assumptions: Model performance stabilizes after sufficient iterations, noise in CV scores is bounded.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When performance plateaus or degrades despite continued exploration.

reasoning_traces.think:
Interaction information τ_ij quantifies how much two features F_i and F_j contribute together toward predicting target Y beyond what either contributes alone. It is defined via entropies and captures synergistic dependencies. In IIFE, τ_ij acts as a cheap yet principled filter for feature pairs, reducing combinatorial explosion compared to brute-force search. This allows scalable automated feature engineering by focusing on high-synergy pairs. The process iteratively applies bivariate transformations B to these pairs, followed by univariate functions U, building increasingly complex features. Each step evaluates candidates using cross-validated performance, selecting those improving model quality. Patience stopping prevents overfitting by halting when performance stagnates. Dualities arise in that τ_ij is symmetric and interpretable as conditional mutual information difference. Failure modes include poor entropy estimation on continuous data, prefiltering dropping XOR-like interactions, and lack of sensitivity analysis on discretization choices. These issues highlight limitations in empirical robustness despite theoretical elegance.
